# Manual on the HMI panel (idea / plan)

Goal: the operating manual is on the machine's Siemens Unified Comfort Panel (10", MTP1000,
1280×800, touch). It's easy to click through, with no zooming or long scrolling. The pages are
**generated by Clipbook**, so nobody writes HTML by hand.

## How it works

1. **Export "Panel"** (GUI button next to "PDF erstellen", or `clipbook panel <machine>`): one offline
   folder per machine (`index.html`, `app.js`, `style.css`, `data.js`, `img/`), all languages inside, chosen
   with `?lang=de`. It only includes the modules this machine has.
   - Each module is a tile; its text is split into pages at the headings (H2 of a component module, H1 of a
     multi-chapter module; long chapters again at the next level).
   - Faults, maintenance and spare parts come from `data.yaml`, not from Word. `{{ABSCHNITT_…}}` markers
     become buttons to those pages.
   - Pictures with text boxes, lines and arrows anchored next to them are rebuilt as one SVG in Word's
     positions, so labels scale with the photo. Shapes far away from any picture become text boxes.
   - **Nothing scrolls.** On the panel, each chapter is cut into screens that fit the space the page
     really gets (measured live, so any Web Control size works): text left, picture right; swipe or
     "Weiter" for the next screen. Lists (chapters, faults, maintenance) are paged with ‹ ›.
   - A slot with `panel: false` in `library.yaml` is left out (e.g. `ce`). Missing translations show the
     German text with a note.
2. **On the panel:** a WinCC Unified **Web Control** on a "Help" screen opens
   `file:///…/index.html`. Siemens confirms that local `file://` works on Unified Comfort Panels,
   but only on the panel itself, not in the web client.
3. **In TIA, once, in the project template:** the Help screen plus a "?" button in the header. The
   same path is used on every machine.

Jump addresses: `index.html?lang=de#/` (start), `#/fault/<code>`, `#/component/<module id>`,
`#/component/<module id>/<page>`, `#/faults`, `#/maintenance`, `#/parts`.

## Error code matching (most important point)

The "?" button should open **the matching fault page directly** for a pending alarm:

```
Alarm 12 pending → "?" → Web Control URL = …/index.html?lang=de#/fault/12
```

This only works if **the alarm number in the PLC/HMI = `code` in the module's `data.yaml`**.

- Settle this **before** building anything else: compare the alarm list from TIA with the
  `faults:` in the library.
- If the numbers differ: add a mapping (e.g. `hmi_alarm: 1012` per fault in `data.yaml`). Don't
  rely on remembering it.
- The same number must not mean different things in different modules (clipper vs. dosing).
  Either use unique numbers per machine or ranges per component.
- The same mechanism works for screens: from the clipper screen, "?" opens `#/component/clipper`.

## Content

- **Start screen:** task tiles (Fault · Maintenance · Operation · Spare parts) and below them the
  component tiles of this machine (icons/colors from the library).
- **Fault:** large number pad for entering a code, plus a list of all faults for this machine.
- **Maintenance / spare parts:** generated from `data.yaml`, not from Word.
- **Word modules:** split at headings into small pages, with "Next →" instead of scrolling.
- **Which content:** set per slot in `library.yaml` (`panel: true/false`). CE/general stay off.
- Last tile: "Full manual (PDF)" as a fallback.

## Rules for the panel

- Touch targets ≥ 60 px (gloves), text ≥ 18–20 px, nothing that relies on hover.
- Fixed buttons for Home / Back / Language on every page (the Web Control has no browser bar).
- Tap an image → fullscreen. Images ≤ 1280 px wide. Convert WMF/EMF to PNG.
- Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, no internet.
- `file://` blocks `fetch()` and `<script type="module">`, so the data is in `data.js`
  (`window.MANUAL = {…}`), loaded with a plain `<script>`.

## Simulator

`../panel-simulator` (separate project, not shipped) shows the panel at real size with a simulated
HMI, alarms and the help pages. It also compares a TIA alarm export against the manual's fault
codes. Its demo (`demo/manual`) is a first draft of what the export should produce.

## Still open

- How the folder gets onto the panel: SD card/USB (exact mount path?), internal storage, or a
  Custom Web Control inside the TIA project. Test on a real panel.
- TIA/Unified version and panel firmware (the `file://` behavior is from the Siemens forum, not the
  manual).
- Are the alarm numbers consistent across all machines? (see above)
- Same idea for screens: which HMI screen belongs to which component (`#/component/clipper`)?
- What does the Web Control do if the script sets the same URL twice (alarm 12, browse, alarm 12
  again)? Test on the real panel.
